jobs.description: At Amazon, our mission is to be Earth’s most customer-centric company. jobs.description: As a Labor Engineering PM II for Workforce Engineering (WFE) within WWGS Operations Business Support, you will execute the core labor engineering process — conducting time studies, performing workflow observations, analyzing task-level data, and developing labor standards that drive accurate staffing models across store formats. You will work closely with store operations teams to observe, measure, and document work processes, translating field observations into data-driven labor standards. This role requires strong analytical rigor, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple concurrent studies while delivering accurate, defensible results that directly impact store-level labor planning. Key job responsibilities Time Studies & Workflow Observation: - Conduct time and motion studies across store departments to establish and validate labor standards - Perform on-site and remote workflow observations to document task sequences, durations, and frequency - Apply appropriate allowance factors (fatigue, personal, delay) to develop fair and accurate standard times - Ensure study methodologies are consistent, repeatable, and statistically sound Labor Standards Development & Maintenance: - Develop, document, and maintain labor standards for assigned store departments or process areas - Analyze task-level data to identify variances between actual and standard performance - Update standards based on process changes, new store formats, or operational shifts - Validate standards through periodic re-observation and data analysis Data Analysis & Reporting: - Perform quantitative analysis on labor data to identify trends, outliers, and opportunities for standards improvement - Build and maintain reporting tools to track standards accuracy and coverage across assigned areas - Present findings and recommendations to team leadership with clear, data-backed rationale Process Documentation & Standardization: - Create and maintain detailed process documentation (SOPs, task breakdowns, flow diagrams) for observed workflows - Ensure documentation is clear, auditable, and accessible to stakeholders - Contribute to WFE's methodology standards to ensure consistency across the team Cross-Functional Collaboration: - Partner with store operations teams to schedule observations, gather context, and validate findings - Coordinate with other Labor Engineers to ensure standards align across departments and formats - Support senior team members on larger-scale projects requiring multi-department analysis

About the role As a Product Strategy and Development Lead , you will serve as the subject-matter expert and oversee the development, implementation, and quality assurance for In-Plan Retirement Income products by providing technical oversight and analytical support of product-related projects. You will interact and collaborate closely with Project and Product Managers within the Product department as well as members from the following functional areas: Information Technology, Marketing, Legal, Operations, Annuity Contract Management, Product Development, Actuarial, Sales Management and other areas of the company involved with product initiatives. Partner with the project manager and cross functional project team to scope and document complex business requirements related to new and in-force product initiatives requiring new/enhanced capabilities. About the Role
As a Technical Deployment Lead on the Forward Deployed Engineering team, you will lead the delivery of custom agentic AI solutions for enterprise customers. You'll own high-value engagements where we collaborate directly with customers to build and deploy agents into their most critical business processes
Each engagement runs from SOW through production deployment. Forward Deployed Engineers build the technical solution; you drive the delivery plan, product scoping, stakeholder relationships, and the organizational complexity of deploying agents into complex enterprise environments.
You need to be credible in architecture conversations with engineering leads and equally comfortable running executive briefings with C-suite sponsors. You won't write production code, but you'll pressure-test technical decisions and make real-time trade-offs on scope and priority when things go sideways on an engagement.
This is also a builder's role. We're in the early innings of an emerging motion - the playbooks, the delivery patterns, the repeatable IP that makes the next engagement faster and better don't exist yet. The TDLs who thrive here are the ones who get that codifying what works is as important as the engagement in front of them right now.
Responsibilities
Own the technical delivery plan for each engagement. Work from the signed SOW to a sequenced roadmap with clear milestones, dependencies, success criteria, and value hypotheses that FDEs execute against.
Lead delivery discovery. Map customer workflows and constraints in depth, pressure-test the scoped MVP against what you find, and shape the solution architecture with the FDEs.
Run day-to-day engineering execution. Drive delivery across Anthropic and customer teams. Keep progress unblocked and sequenced. Make real-time trade-offs on scope and priority to protect the critical path.
Own product scoping during delivery. Author requirements, prioritize the engineering backlog, manage scope against success criteria, and hold the bar for what good looks like for the people and enterprises who will use the product.
Own the customer relationship throughout delivery. Lead executive briefings, manage stakeholder communications across technical leads and procurement, and represent Anthropic's technical credibility with senior business and engineering leaders.
Own value measurement and ROI. Define impact hypotheses, set baselines and KPIs, run pre- and post-deployment measurement, and report outcomes to executive sponsors.
Contribute reusable delivery patterns. Capture what works on your engagements and feed field signal to the Programs Leads, Product, and Research.
Navigate enterprise and regulatory complexity. Security reviews, legal approvals, procurement processes, compliance requirements, and organizational dynamics.
Manage scope and change. Handle evolving requirements, set expectations, negotiate contract modifications, identify risks early, and escalate with clear context when needed.
Run engagement-level delivery operations: sprint ceremonies, milestone reviews, and engagement reporting that feed the team's post-sales cadence and dashboards.
Travel to customer sites. Build relationships, unblock delivery, and accelerate adoption. (up to 25–50% travel expected).

Have led AI/ML engagements/deployments, whether as a founder, data scientist, engineer, researcher, or in a professional services or consulting role.
Operate like the CEO of your engagement. You take initiative without a mandate, make decisions with incomplete information, and lead rather than wait for instructions.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's Business Technology Engineering team builds the systems the company runs on. We own the internal platforms every employee uses and our collaboration tooling, and we embed engineers directly with Legal, Security, Communications, Product Operations and other business functions to rebuild how their work gets done with Claude at the center. Our mandate is to make Anthropic the best-run company in the world at using its own models internally, and to be the example our customers point to.
We are hiring an engineering leader to run this org. You will lead a growing engineering organization across two tracks:
Platforms
, which builds and operates the shared systems the company depends on, and
Forward Deployed
, which drops into a business function, proves Claude wins on a real workflow, hands off, and moves on. You will partner on defining the roadmap, build relationships with functional leaders, grow the team, and shape what forward deployed engineering looks like inside a frontier AI lab.
You'll report to the Head of Business Technology and IT, within the Security organization, and you’ll make up the full Business Technology function along with a team of Business Systems Analysts and Product Managers. Together, BizTech partners closely with IT Engineering on corporate systems and endpoints; with Security Engineering on data handling and permissions for agentic workflows; with Labs and Product on dogfooding and the internal builds that become external patterns; with GTM, who point Enterprise customers at this team as the reference for how Anthropic runs internally; and with the leaders of Legal, Workplace, Communications, Product Operations and Product Support, who are your customers.
Responsibilities
Lead and scale a global org of engineers; hire, level and develop the leads under you.
Partner, develop, and execute a year-plus roadmap for how Anthropic's business functions work with Claude, and the success metrics that go with it.
Run the Platforms track: reliability, velocity and scale of Claude Support and the platform layer that every employee depends on.
Run the Forward Deployed track: engagement portfolio, prioritization across functions, handoffs to durable owners, and adoption that actually moves.
Be the technical executive partner to the leaders of Legal, Workplace, Comms, Product Ops and Product Support; make the case for ambitious deployment and for the boundaries on it in the same conversation.
Partner with Labs and Product on dogfooding: feed load-bearing signal back ("here is the eval that shows the gap") and ship internal builds that become external product patterns.
Represent how Anthropic runs internally to Enterprise customers alongside GTM.
Set the engineering bar: production-adjacent builds, eval rigor, reusable patterns, responsible internal deployment with real data and real permissions.
You may be a good fit if you
Have 12+ years in software engineering and 6+ years leading engineers, including at least 3 years managing managers and at least one org of 20+ across multiple domains that you structured yourself
Have run internal-tools, business-systems or platform engineering at a company that added functions faster than it added engineers, and can speak to reliability outcomes on the platform side and adoption outcomes on the embedded side
Lead through technical judgment: whether or not you've been hands-on lately, you can go from an agent architecture to its eval design to its failure modes with your engineers, and your reviews make their builds better
Can walk a General Counsel, a Head of Workplace or a room of senior engineers with strong opinions through a trade-off, make a recommendation, and bring them to a decision they'll commit to
Can hold a high bar on craft while saying no to low-leverage work, and explain the no to the person who asked.
Want real ownership of how a frontier AI lab runs itself on its own models, and care about doing that responsibly — real data, real permissions, real people on the other end

Forward deployed, software engineering or applied AI leadership experience with external customers.
Product management experience or a track record partnering closely with PMs and analysts.
Experience with corporate systems (Salesforce, Workday, Google Workspace, Slack) at platform scale.
Have built the career rubric or leveling framework for a new kind of engineering role, or stood up a forward deployed function from zero

We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. anthropic.com/careers

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

jobs.description: GHR AI Engineer – Agentic Integrations (MCP / A2A / Python / APIs) Corporate Functions Technology Reports to: Managing Director, Corporate Functions Technology Role Overview The GHR AI Engineer – Agentic Integrations will help build and integrate employee-facing AI capabilities by connecting a custom React intranet experience to internal AI services and to external vendor agents. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on building the “integration layer” for agentic systems: Python services, APIs, connectors, tool definitions, and secure runtime patterns that allow agents to take actions and retrieve knowledge safely. The ideal candidate has strong Python fundamentals, comfort with APIs and authentication, and practical experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent collaboration patterns. You will partner closely with front-end engineers, solution architects, cybersecurity, and platform teams to deliver secure, scalable AI integrations that improve employee experience (with GHR/HR domain knowledge as a plus). Key Responsibilities Agentic Integration Engineering (MCP + A2A) • Build and maintain MCP-based connectors that expose internal tools and data sources to AI agents in a consistent, secure way (tools/resources/prompts). • Implement agent-to-agent interaction patterns for multi-step workflows where agents coordinate across internal systems and external vendor agents. • Define tool contracts (schemas, parameters, outputs), versioning, and compatibility practices for long-term maintainability. Internal AI Gateway & Vendor Agent Connectivity • Integrate your intranet and internal platforms with the enterprise AI gateway and approved LLM/agent runtimes. • Connect to external vendors that provide agents or agent-accessible capabilities (via MCP or API-based tool calling) while enforcing authentication, authorization, and auditing requirements. • Implement safe, reliable request routing patterns (timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, fallbacks) and error-handling standards. API & Backend Development (Python) • Develop lightweight Python services that broker requests between the React intranet and agent runtimes/tools. • Build and maintain REST APIs (and/or async workers) that support agent workflows, tool execution, and structured responses back to the UI. • Support data shaping and transformation (JSON, schemas, normalization) to make multi-source responses usable for employee-facing experiences.
